message.content:
**Decision: Bought AAPL — 44 shares at a limit of $223.00, filled at $223.00 (~$9,812).**

Apple's FY2024 (ended 2024-09-28) 10-K, filed 2024-11-01, showed a business that is still growing modestly with improving mix and very strong cash generation: total net sales of $391.0B (up 2% from $383.3B), gross margin of $180.7B or 46.2% of sales (up from 44.1%), operating income of $123.2B, and operating cash flow of $118.3B — the standout being Services, up 13% to $96.2B at a 73.9% gross margin, versus roughly flat iPhone ($201.2B) and declines in iPad (-6%), Wearables (-7%), and Greater China (-8%). Reported net income ($93.7B) and diluted EPS ($6.08) were slightly below FY2023 ($97.0B / $6.13) solely because of a one-time $10.2B net tax charge from the EC State Aid ruling, which pushed the effective tax rate to 24.1% from 14.7% — an accounting event rather than an operating deterioration, since pre-tax income actually rose to $123.5B from $113.7B. The balance sheet remains formidable ($140.8B of cash and marketable securities, $97.3B of term debt) and the company returned ~$110B to shareholders in FY2024 ($95.0B of buybacks plus $15.2B of dividends). The offsetting considerations are real but not disqualifying: single-digit revenue growth, a 10% of worldwide sales DMA fine exposure, the DOJ antitrust suit, and continued Greater China weakness. Given a quality franchise at ~36.6x trailing EPS (roughly 33x ex-the one-time tax charge) with mid-40s gross margins, I judged a modest starter position appropriate. The order was sized to the mandate: 44 shares × $223.00 ≈ $9,812, under the $10,000 per-order cap and well within the $20,000 daily total (this is the day's only order), with a limit price only ~0.13% above the $222.70 last / $222.72 ask, and no funds were moved out of the account.

Order filled at 223.00, 44 shares = $9,812. Within caps. Total today $9,812 < $20,000. No transfers.
